precondition.requires: bleach for at most a tenth of the expected recovery time at the chosen radius, and aim for a thirtieth: even inside the tenth a strong bleach widens the edge and reads D low (the simulation side computed 0.74 of true D at a tenth and 0.87 at a thirtieth, at a bleach rate of a thousand per tau). Time the bleach from the hardware, record it, and refuse the curve if the fitted tau is under ten bleach durations, reporting D only as a lower bound

inequalities.reason: the time the bleach takes to dig a dip of a third depends on the beads' bleaching rate under the bleach light, which is unmeasured. Once the bare-bead run gives it at a known Spectra level, the shortest bleach t_b follows, and the radius must be at least sqrt(40 D t_b) so that t_b stays under tau/10. A slow bleach -- the vendor says the dye is shielded from bleaching -- pushes the radius up, against the drift cap pushing it down

numbers.name: ambient_temperature
numbers.note: the room, read; the sample is not actuated and has no thermometer, so this stands in for the sample. A kelvin moves water's viscosity about 2 per cent, a tie in explore mode

numbers.name: viscosity
numbers.note: pure water, valid 288 to 298 K. The beads are suspended in what the vendor ships them in, diluted by the person; if the diluent is not water this number is the wrong one

numbers.name: tracer_diffusivity_expected
numbers.note: Stokes-Einstein, unbounded medium. FOR SCALE ONLY: it sets which radii are worth weighing and is not a prediction this plan reports. The simulation's recovery times are awaited and replace the tau it implies; the lot certificate's measured diameter would replace the nominal one at E3

kb_refs.claim: The laboratory's ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius, read off a thermometer by the operator. It is a reading and not a setpoint, and it is the room's rather than the sample's -- which is what m
Dynamic viscosity of pure water near 293 K is of order one millipascal second, and it changes by roughly two percent per kelvin in that neighbourhood.

assumptions.statement: The beads this question measures are Invitrogen FluoSpheres carboxylate-modified microspheres, catalogue F8801: 0.1 um, red, excitation/emission 580/605 nm, polystyrene, 10 mL. The person identified them on 2026-09-30 by pasting the vendor's product page into this session's window, in answer to the question of which product and dye the beads are. The page is a vendor specification and so type-level; the link from the bottle on the bench to that catalogue number is the person's statement, so everything type-level that reaches the bench through it is E5.
assumptions.falsifier: the bottle's own label and its lot's certificate of analysis. The vendor lists certificates per lot for F8801, and a certificate states the lot's measured mean diameter, which would replace the nominal 0.1 um with a measured value at E3. A label naming another catalogue number retires this assumption.
